method: Compared every candidate responsibility, input, output, permission identity, trigger cases, anti-trigger routes, and distinctive gate against its Phase 2 capability and hand-authored semantic design.
Computed pairwise lexical overlap across should-trigger corpora; no pair met the 0.28 Jaccard review threshold.
Audited all anti-routes for known capability targets and all read-only plan-review execution identities for absence of write tools.
Verified Phase 9 evidence remains explicitly not-run and holdout cases are physically distinct from authored trigger cases.

resolved_findings.finding: Initial candidate contracts inherited broad legacy Phase 2 cluster responsibilities and gates, allowing adjacent research or persona work to remain in problem framing.
resolved_findings.resolution: Candidate responsibility and hard gates now come from the Phase 3 semantic design; Phase 2 contract text remains provenance only.

resolved_findings.finding: Initial evaluation plans reused authored trigger and anti-trigger IDs as holdouts.
resolved_findings.resolution: Added a separate 62-case holdout corpus with unseen paraphrases and disjoint IDs; evaluation plans reference only this corpus.

resolved_findings.finding: Boundary and authority fixtures initially used two generic placeholder prompts for every Skill.
resolved_findings.resolution: Boundary prompts now embed each Skill's atomic outcome; authority prompts branch by data governance, named formula, human decision, or downstream/external action boundary.

resolved_findings.finding: The requirements candidate initially named a draft V1 Slot and nonexistent version as a released baseline.
resolved_findings.resolution: It now uses the source Skill baseline; the Gate independently proves every claimed released baseline exists at the exact released version.

resolved_findings.finding: The compiler initially removed the manual semantic review artifact while regenerating schema files.
resolved_findings.resolution: Compiler cleanup is limited to the generated candidate root; manual semantic evidence under curation/v2/phase-3 is preserved.

boundary_samples.boundary: Problem framing classifies supplied problem evidence without solution content; hypothesis design starts only from a validated problem and produces a falsifiable mechanism and experiment contract.
Qualitative synthesis codes governed observations into themes and counterexamples; opportunity synthesis integrates heterogeneous evidence and may issue a bounded ranking recommendation.
Named-framework scoring declares exact formulas and sensitivity; roadmap construction begins from approved outcomes and preserves human selection and decision gates.

Research planning defines authorization, consent, sampling, minimization, retention, transfer, and deletion without contacting participants; interview execution operates only under that approved contract.
General traceability review, design-state review, developer-journey review, and strategic executive review remain distinct read-only lenses; none edits or approves the plan.
Requirements define observable product behavior and acceptance; implementation planning consumes approved behavior to sequence work and verification without resolving product ambiguity.
Intake chooses one next capability from a request; orchestration composes already selected atomic contracts into conditional stateful workflows and still performs no downstream work.
Both produce evidence-bounded recommendations, but GO/PIVOT/KILL, strategic selection, scope approval, and build approval remain explicit human decisions.

release_claim: none; all 31 candidates remain evaluating and all evaluation plans remain not-run-phase-9
